sn35.69:1.1: The commentary says this was Upasena son of Vaṅgantā, Sāriputta’s younger brother. When newly ordained, he made the mistake of ordaining students too early ([pli-tv-kd1:31.3.2]()), but later developed an impressive following ([pli-tv-bu-vb-np15:1.1.9]()), leading the Buddha to declare him the foremost of those who were “impressive all around” ([an1.213]()). His song of triumph is recorded at [ud4.9](), while his verses at [thag10.6]() focus on contentment and humility.
sn35.69:1.4: This illustrates the difference between _bāhira_ (“exterior”) and _bahiddha_ (“external, outside”). _Bāhira_ is the outside of an organism or a single thing (such as an altar), whereas _bahiddha_ is something outside a point of reference or removed past a boundary. That is, interior/exterior are two aspects of a single thing, whereas inside/outside are two distinct things.
